title: Letter of Instruction Outline
description: An outline for an informal letter that tells your family where things are, who to call, and what matters to you.
intro: A letter of instruction is not a legal document, but it fills the gaps a will leaves. It tells your family the practical details in your own words. Use these headings as a starting point and update the letter whenever things change.

sections.heading: Where to find things
items: Location of your original will, trust, and powers of attorney
Location of your asset and account inventory
Location of keys, safe combinations, and safe deposit box
Location of tax returns from recent years
Location of birth, marriage, and military discharge papers

sections.heading: People to contact
items: Your estate planning attorney
Your accountant or tax preparer
Your financial advisor
Your insurance agent
Your employer or benefits office
Close friends who should be told

sections.heading: Practical matters
items: Bills that are paid automatically and from which account
Care instructions for pets
Home maintenance details, such as alarm codes and service providers
Vehicles and where titles and keys are kept
Subscriptions and memberships to cancel

sections.heading: Personal wishes
items: Funeral and burial or cremation wishes
Who should receive personal items with sentimental value
Stories or family history you want passed on
Messages to children, grandchildren, or friends

sections.heading: Keeping it current
items: Date the letter each time you update it
Store it with your estate planning documents
Tell your executor where it is
Review it once a year
